nodes.description: HER performance in neutral 0.1 M sodium phosphate electrolyte (pH 7.2) under silent conditions
nodes.source_text: Linear sweep voltammograms (LSV) for HER in neutral 0.1 M Na2HPO4/NaH2PO4 electrolyte (pH 7.2) on polycrystalline Au under silent conditions... Tafel slope from 0.480 V dec−1 under silent conditions... at −1 V, the current density... from −11.8 to −164.4 mA cm−2.

nodes.description: HER performance in neutral 0.1 M sodium phosphate (pH 7.2) with SRBW 20 dBm
nodes.source_text: with 20 dBm SRBW, the system requires a 0.2 V overpotential to reach a current density of −1 mA cm−2... For −10 mA cm−2, the requisite overpotential of 0.4 V... overpotential is reduced... 0.52 and 1.37 V for current densities of −10 and −100 mA cm−2... Tafel slope... 0.184 V dec−1... current density increases by ≈14-fold... from −11.8 to −164.4 mA cm−2.

nodes.description: HER stability test in neutral electrolyte with SRBW
nodes.source_text: the electrolytic reaction under the SRBW was extremely stable, as confirmed by the chronopotentiometry results over 6 h in Figure S9.

nodes.description: HER performance on polycrystalline Ag with SRBW excitation in neutral electrolyte
nodes.source_text: experiments performed using silver as the working electrode instead of gold... yield similar increases in electrocatalytic performance and trends under the SRBW excitation, namely a reduction in the overpotential coupled with an increase in current density (Figure S4, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: X-ray diffraction pattern confirms polycrystalline nature of the Au electrode (Figure S1).
nodes.evidence_snippet: on polycrystalline gold Au electrodes (as confirmed by the x-ray diffraction pattern in Figure S1, Supporting Information)

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms absence of Pt deposition on the Au working electrode (Figure S6).
nodes.evidence_snippet: absence of any evidence of Pt deposition on the Au working electrode, as confirmed from the X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) measurements on the electrode in Figure S6 (Supporting Information)

nodes.characterization_summary: Deconvoluted Raman spectra (3000-3800 cm⁻¹) show SRBW excitation increases 'free' water peak (3624 cm⁻¹) by 61.3% and decreases rigid tetrahedral water peak by 25.4% at -8 mA cm⁻² at Au electrode-electrolyte interface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 4a,b shows results from the Raman spectra across the wavenumber range 3000 - 3800 cm⁻¹ corresponding to the hydrogen bond structure of the water molecules at the electrode-electrolyte interface under both silent and in situ SRBW conditions.
